judged_text: The multi-host destination state exists only in memory: the Booking row persists a single destinationCalendar via `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`, so only the first host's destination survives creation. Every downstream flow in this very diff that rebuilds evt from the booking row — bookingReminder cron, handleCancelBooking, confirm/editLocation/paypal handlers — constructs a one-element array from booking.destinationCalendar, so the multi-host destination set is enforced only during create and is unrecoverable later except by reverse-engineering booking references.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` an array and in `handleNewBooking` explicitly appends team members’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the Booking it still connects only a single destination calendar: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (no loop / no join table), so the additional destinations are not stored on the Booking row. Later flows shown in the diff rebuild `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` by wrapping it into a 1-element array (e.g. bookingReminder cron, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, confirm/editLocation/cancel handlers), meaning those downstream paths cannot recover the multi-destination set from the Booking record (they’d have to infer it from references). This is verifiable state loss/inconsistency introduced by the change.
